events.say: Baarish aayi... baarish aayi... mitti ki khushboo laayi...
Hmm hmm hmm... la la la...
Arrey baba! Proper rain today!
Okay, one-three-three. Show me what you saw today.
Dry inside. Battery full... and there, the blink. Still talking to the next station.
Temperature... humidity... rain, fourteen millimetres...
All correct.
Perfect readings. Good boy.
Mark? It's six in the morning in Texas...
Deepak! Thank God. Are you watching the news?

stick_screen.headline: HURRICANE DELIA SLAMS TEXAS COAST
stick_screen.ticker: UV index 14 in Austin · Ozone alert for twelve states · Schools closed in Houston

events.say: Hurricane Delia has made landfall in Texas, months before the hurricane season.
Forecasters say they have never seen a storm grow this fast.
Turn it up... That's twenty miles from my lab.
The whole coast is under water, Deepak. And the UV readings... they make no sense.
It's pouring here too, Mark. But my station is fine. Everything reads normal.
Our UV sensors jumped forty percent overnight. Ten sensors. I sent you everything on WhatsApp.
Ten sensors can't all be wrong...
Promise me you'll look at it tonight. It's important.
I promise. I'll call you back.
Deepak! In this rain? Are you mad?
The station is fine. It's the rest of the world I'm worried about.
Look at you! Wet like a fish!
Station one-three-three is online, Raghav. And something is very wrong with the weather.
Come home. Eat first. Save the world after dinner.
All right, Mark. Let's see what you found.

stick_screen.title: WhatsApp · 312 unread
messages: Your station 47 shows UV way above normal. Ours too.
Bahut garmi, phir achanak thand. Kya ho raha hai?
Storm forming near Recife. Nothing like it in our records.
Deepak, look beyond the official reports. The patterns don't make sense.

events.say: Three hundred and twelve messages? Farmers... researchers... Rao from the weather office...
They're all saying the same thing.
UV index twelve. In March.
Ozone dropping. Temperature jumping. This is not one bad sensor.
You see it now? Look at the Atlantic. And the Pacific. Cyclones forming at the same time.
El Niño is getting stronger. Heat here, sudden cold there... It's everywhere, Mark.
That's why I called you first.
This can't be happening everywhere. Something is wrong with these readings... or something is happening that we don't understand.
No more guessing. I need proof.
Station forty-seven... offline? It never goes offline.
Fifty kilometres. I can be there in an hour.
Melted. From the inside.
This was not lightning. Something burned it out from the inside.
Headlights? Out here? At this hour?
Who's there?!
Come on, come on, come on!
They're gone...
Who knows about station forty-seven? Who else is watching my network?

stick_screen.title: Deepak's LoRa network · compared with satellite data

events.say: Day four. Station forty-seven. Station eighty-eight. The same jump, every night.
And the government archives for those dates... empty. Who deleted them?
Hello? Who is this?
Deepak? My name is Carlos. I'm calling from Panama. I heard you're investigating the atmospheric anomalies.
Who told you that?
That doesn't matter. Some of the data I've collected isn't public. I think you need to see it.
What exactly have you found?
I'm sending you a document. Read page three. Carefully.

stick_screen.title: Long-Term Crisis Scenarios
lines: 2. Projected disruption to food production and infrastructure
4. Under extreme combined disasters, large populations may lose reliable food, water, electricity and habitable land.

events.say: Continuity of population... deep shelters... ten thousand people?
They're not just studying how to survive disasters. They're thinking about how people could survive if the systems supporting civilization stopped working.
That's why I contacted you. You understand weather, electronics, remote monitoring, and how to build systems that work on their own.
My little weather boxes... part of something this big?
Two hours of sleep... Okay. Okay.
Deepak! Your tea is getting cold!
Two minutes, Raghav! Two minutes!
Did you sleep at all? Your eyes look like tomatoes.
The numbers kept me awake. Hail in March, Raghav. UV forty percent up in Texas.
Texas is far away. Here, the cows still want breakfast.
Cars? Who comes here at this hour?
Check the back. Nobody leaves.
Deepak... who are these people?
Mr. Deepak Meena?
Yes. Who's asking?
Agent Rathore. Ministry of Home Affairs. You need to come with us. Now.
Now? What has he done? He fixes weather boxes!
Stay back, sir!
Raghav, stop! It's okay. It's okay.
Government business, sir. Please stay inside.
Am I under arrest?
No, sir. Consider it an invitation. One you cannot decline.
My stations... my data...
Your data is already in Delhi, Mr. Meena. We have been reading it for weeks.
Raghav, look after the stations. I'll call you.
Deepak! Call me when you get there!
Look after the stations, Raghav!
Hold on!
Lightning hit the tree! In this season?!
Go around it. Nobody stops. Delhi by noon.
The Ministry? For a few weather stations?
Not for your stations, Mr. Meena. For what they found.
This way. Keep your head down. There are cameras everywhere.
Welcome to Room Seven. Officially, this room does not exist.
What is this place? Why am I here?
Because your little weather stations saw what our satellites missed. I'm Dr. Kavya Iyer, climate division.
You've been watching my network?
One hundred and thirty three stations, Mr. Meena. Every reading. Every night you stayed awake.
And this is Mr. Verma. He decides what the country is told... and what it is not.
Sit down, Mr. Meena. Everything said in this room is classified. Do you understand?
I understand. But if this is real, people deserve to know.
People deserve the truth when we are sure of it. Panic can kill faster than any storm.
Mr. Meena, we have reviewed your work. We want you to explain your findings in your own words.
I'll tell you which data I trust, which readings may be faulty, and which patterns need more study.
I cannot tell you that the world will end. No honest scientist can. But we should prepare for scenarios that most people don't want to consider.
And what do you think we should do?
We need to think much bigger.
A deep underground settlement. Not a bunker with a few rooms. A complete community, designed for ten thousand people.
Its own water, protected food production, renewable and backup power, a hospital, workshops, communications, recycling.
About a hundred metres down, if the geology, groundwater and ventilation studies allow it.
Not just a shelter. A way to keep everything we know alive.
When do you think we might need something like this?
It could be unnecessary for a hundred years. Or a serious crisis could arrive within ten. The point is not to wait until we have no time left.
If we approved your proposal, what would you need?
Five hundred acres of land. A secure research facility. Engineers, geologists, climate scientists, doctors, farmers, systems designers. And the freedom to build a prototype first.
And you believe you can lead this project?
I can lead the technical vision. But no one person can build this alone. If we do it, we do it properly.
We will evaluate your proposal. If approved, it stays confidential. And unverified conclusions must never be shared as facts.
Mr. Meena. Your proposal is approved. Five hundred acres. Code name: Deep Earth.
Ten thousand people... by twenty thirty-five. Thank you, sir.
Don't thank me yet. Start digging.
The rock is solid here. We start the survey from this corner.
And if the villagers ask?
Tell them I'm fixing weather sensors. That's what I always do.
A hundred metres down? Are you sure about this, Deepak?
Cranes by summer. Tunnels by winter. We don't stop.
Sir! The wall... it's cracking!
Watch out!
Grab my hand! Come on!
Thank you, sir... thank you.
The ground is too soft here. Move the shaft fifty metres north. Nobody digs here again.
The lift goes down here. The first tunnel here. Then we keep digging.
Day and night?
Day and night.
One day, ten thousand people will walk through here.
Let's hope they never need to.
Mark? It's two in the morning...
Deepak, there's something else you need to see. The latest data just came in.
Open the global map. Thousands of stations.
Look. Several stopped transmitting at the same moment. The exact same moment.
No... this isn't possible.
That's not a cloud...
Deepak! What is that? The whole sky is moving!
The power... the whole village just went dark!
That's what my stations were trying to tell us.
Twenty thirty-five... might be much too late.
If my stations are right...
...this is what's coming.
